import numpy as np

# 1. Log of total commercial rateable value (proxy for local business assets, skewed distribution)
df['log_voa_rv_2023'] = np.log1p(df['VOA_total_RV_million_2023'])
# Useful as a scalable proxy for business asset value in the area.

# 2. Business asset value per working age resident (normalizes for population structure)
df['rv_per_working_age'] = df['VOA_total_RV_million_2023'] / (df['Working_Age_Pop'] + 1)
# Helps interpret asset value relative to productive population.

# 3. SME density (local units per 1k residents, reflects enterprise dynamism)
df['sme_density'] = df['LU_total_2025_msoa'] / (df['Total_Pop_Mid2024'] / 1000)
# Useful for measuring business density, a likely GVA driver.

# 4. Share of micro and small businesses combined (captures SME business structure)
df['pct_micro_small'] = df['LU_pct_micro_2025_msoa'] + df['LU_pct_small_2025_msoa']
# SME structure is important for local economic resilience and value added.

# 5. Employment rate (core economic activity indicator)
df['employment_rate'] = df['employment_rate_per_pop']
# Already normalized, direct measure of labour market participation.

# 6. Workforce qualification index (linear combination: L4+ - No quals, higher is better)
df['qualification_index'] = df['Level 4 qualifications or above: degree (BA, BSc), higher degree (MA, PhD, PGCE), NVQ level 4 to 5, HNC, HND, RSA Higher Diploma, BTEC Higher level, professional qualifications (for example, teaching, nursing, accountancy) %'] - df['No qualifications %']
# Captures net upskilling in the area, likely correlates with productivity.

# 7. Enterprise sector diversity (1-HHI across firm size, more diverse = more resilient, dynamic)
df['firm_size_diversity'] = df['LU_diversity_1-HHI_2025']
# High diversity in firm size may buffer shocks and support innovation.

# 8. Share of knowledge-intensive business services (KIBS) (proxy for advanced/modern sector)
df['share_kibs'] = df['share_enterprises_kibs_2025_msoa']
# KIBS are typically high value-added and innovation intensive.

# 9. Change in business asset value, 2023-2026 (%)
df['rv_pct_change'] = df['VOA_total_RV_pct_change']
# Indicates recent/future business investment and optimism.

# 10. Full-time to part-time employment ratio (labour market quality and wage structure)
df['full_to_part_ratio'] = df['full_to_part_ratio']
# High ratios may indicate more stable and productive employment.

# Now drop all other columns to keep only the 10 engineered/selected features
df = df[['log_voa_rv_2023',
         'rv_per_working_age',
         'sme_density',
         'pct_micro_small',
         'employment_rate',
         'qualification_index',
         'firm_size_diversity',
         'share_kibs',
         'rv_pct_change',
         'full_to_part_ratio'
        ]]

import numpy as np

# --- 1. Asset value per SME: local asset intensity per enterprise ---
df['asset_per_sme'] = np.exp(df['log_voa_rv_2023']) / (df['sme_density'] + 1)
# This feature captures the average business asset value per SME (proxy for capital intensity per firm).

# --- 2. Interaction: Qualifications x KIBS share (skilled KIBS concentration) ---
df['skilled_kibs_index'] = df['qualification_index'] * df['share_kibs']
# High-value KIBS sectors are most productive with a skilled workforce; this interaction captures that effect.

# --- 3. SME Density x Employment Rate (enterprise-driven employment) ---
df['sme_employment_interaction'] = df['sme_density'] * df['employment_rate']
# Indicates how densely populated SMEs are contributing to local employment rates.

# --- 4. Asset growth x KIBS share (forward-looking modern sector investment) ---
df['kibs_asset_growth'] = df['rv_pct_change'] * df['share_kibs']
# Captures whether advanced sectors are located in areas expecting business asset growth.

# --- 5. Full-to-part-time ratio x Qualifications (quality employment mix) ---
df['quality_employment_index'] = df['full_to_part_ratio'] * df['qualification_index']
# Combines employment structure and skills to proxy for quality of local jobs.

# --- 6. Log of SME density (normalize, reduce skew) ---
df['log_sme_density'] = np.log1p(df['sme_density'])
# Reduces skew and enables non-linear effects for enterprise density.

# --- 7. Firm size diversity x asset value per working-age (diversity-weighted asset base) ---
df['diversity_weighted_asset'] = df['firm_size_diversity'] * df['rv_per_working_age']
# Captures whether areas with diverse firm sizes also have high per-capita business asset value.

# --- 8. Micro/small business share x asset value per working-age (SME asset leverage) ---
df['micro_small_asset_leverage'] = df['pct_micro_small'] * df['rv_per_working_age']
# Indicates whether areas dominated by small firms also have high asset intensity per worker.

# --- 9. Drop original columns that have been combined or superseded by interactions ---
drop_cols = [

    'rv_per_working_age',      # replaced by diversity_weighted_asset, micro_small_asset_leverage

    'employment_rate',         # replaced by sme_employment_interaction
    'qualification_index',     # replaced by skilled_kibs_index, quality_employment_index
    'firm_size_diversity',     # replaced by diversity_weighted_asset
    'share_kibs',              # replaced by skilled_kibs_index, kibs_asset_growth
    'rv_pct_change',           # replaced by kibs_asset_growth
    'full_to_part_ratio'       # replaced by quality_employment_index
]
df.drop(columns=drop_cols, inplace=True)

# --- 10. Final feature set: keep only 10 features (all engineered) ---
df = df[[
    'asset_per_sme',
    'skilled_kibs_index',
    'sme_employment_interaction',
    'kibs_asset_growth',
    'quality_employment_index',
